title: RAW INCOMPLETE: a medial verb inflection carries its first or second participant into the next clause
summary: Invented short factual clauses end in a productive verb form that says either keep the same first participant, carry the just-written second participant, or end the chain. The next clause omits only the participant explicitly selected by that preceding ending. Ordinary kind words and exact proper names introduce all other participants. This gives a complete restricted Roman teaching grammar with fewer separate reference/control words, not a complete22-working-sign writer. A fixed nonempty word-final SAME exponent already faces a conditional native triple-terminal obstruction; no allomorph or carrier repair is added. No native word has a meaning and no experiment is recommended.

purpose_and_domain.hand_rule: At the end of a predicate, write which of its two available participants is the topic of the next clause. The writer then need not repeat that same noun phrase. A separate chain-ending inflection makes the next clause introduce its subject afresh.
purpose_and_domain.input: An ordered chain of present/atemporal factual assertions, each using one taught unary predicate or one taught ordered binary relation. Participants are either explicitly supplied named constants or newly existentially introduced instances of a learned nominal kind. A following clause may reuse exactly the preceding clause's first participant or second participant. Any additional anonymous identity link outside that small scope is not silently supplied.
purpose_and_domain.no_extra_content: Written order is assertion order, not temporal succession or causal order. No action command, tense, modality, count, comparison degree, collective/distributive plural, conditional or quantifier scope is supplied for free. The teaching lexicon and examples are factual descriptions only. Historical text outside that domain needs another declared grammar; no complete medical-text coverage is claimed.
purpose_and_domain.difference_from956: There is no walking relation cursor, stack, branch opening or return. An ordinary predicate consumes its stated1or2 arguments and asserts a relation. Its inflection selects one of those SAME arguments as the next clause's first argument. Moving to the second argument loses direct access to an unnamed first argument; the language does not recreate it by an unspoken branch return.
purpose_and_domain.semantic_inverse_ceiling: The reader recovers the ordered clauses, lexical identities, argument positions, exact names, existential kind restrictions, predicate negations and explicit carried identity. The reader does not recover original ordinary-language wording, truth, hidden tense, particular unnamed identities or distinctions outside the input domain.

open_lexicon_and_inflection.roots: Roman teaching roots are nonempty lowercase a-z strings. Root spellings are learned, not numeric dictionary addresses. Each nominal use pays its kind predicate; each verbal use pays its unary or ordered binary predicate. The same spelling may have separately taught nominal and verbal uses because the visible verb inflection distinguishes them. No free zero-derivation meaning is inferred from spelling.

three_inflections.~s: Close this predicate clause and require a next clause whose first participant is exactly this clause's first participant S.
three_inflections.~o: Close this predicate clause and require a next clause whose first participant is exactly this clause's second participant O. Legal only on a binary predicate, whose O was actually written in this clause.
three_inflections.~e: Close this predicate clause and the chain. Clear the inherited-participant slot; a next chain must write a new first participant explicitly.

open_lexicon_and_inflection.verb_word: A complete finite word is ROOT~s, ROOT~o or ROOT~e, optionally preceded by one ! for predicate negation. The tilde, ending letter and optional exclamation are written parts of that same teaching word. No period or separate clause-control word is required or inferred.
open_lexicon_and_inflection.meaning_of_roles: S and O are ordered argument positions, not universally agent and patient. For a comparison, the lexicon pays which is comparator and standard; for a property only S exists. ~o never means an arbitrary recently mentioned thing, and matching noun shape does not choose the controller.
open_lexicon_and_inflection.open_vocabulary_cost: Every genuinely new common kind or predicate still needs a taught spelling, definition and appropriate valency. The language does not reduce an open lexicon to a handful of universal concepts. A foreign proper name can preserve an unfamiliar spelling; it cannot convey an unfamiliar common-word or predicate meaning by itself.
open_lexicon_and_inflection.word_formation_limit: Only the declared verb inflection and polarity are productive here. Internal repeated substrings and longer lexical compounds have no automatic plural, intensity or iterative meaning. An independently learned root with repeated letters is allowed, with its ordinary lexical cost. No native root or suffix is inferred.

full_teaching_grammar.NP: One bare taught nominal root or one quoted exact proper name. Bare nominal occurrences introduce fresh existential variables of their taught kind; fresh variable names do not impose inequality. Repeating a bare nominal does not by itself mean the same object. A proper name supplies its named constant.
full_teaching_grammar.initial_clause: Write one complete NP for S. If the closing predicate is binary, write exactly one further NP for O; if unary, write no O. Then write the complete finite predicate word with one of the three inflections. No other words intervene. Two NPs followed by a unary predicate, or one NP followed by a binary predicate, are invalid.
full_teaching_grammar.carried_clause: After ~s or ~o the first participant is already explicitly selected by the previous inflection and MUST NOT be written again. Write exactly one new NP iff the next predicate is binary; write none if unary. Then write its full finite predicate word. The predicate's learned valency determines the required NP count; a wrong count is an error, not an ellipsis to guess.
full_teaching_grammar.text: One or more chains. Every chain ends in ~e. After ~s or ~o, end of message is an error because the promised following clause is absent. Physical lines and paragraphs do not close a chain or reset the carried identity. There are no implicit subject defaults at the start of a message or chain.
full_teaching_grammar.parse: Read complete NPs until a tilde-bearing finite word. The tilde cannot appear in a root and is protected inside quoted names. Determine the predicate's valency and check exactly the required NP count according to whether an inherited S is active. Bind arguments in their written order, assert or negate the predicate, and update the one inherited slot from its suffix. This does not require choosing the nearest matching ending or a hidden source sentence boundary.
full_teaching_grammar.negation: ! negates only the just-written predicate application P(S) or R(S,O). Explicit nominal-kind introductions remain existentially asserted outside that negation, so their entities can be carried into the next clause even when the relation is denied. There is no outer NOT-EXISTS construction. For example an object word followed by !touch~o asserts that the object exists and is not touched by S; it does not deny that any such object exists.
full_teaching_grammar.identity: ~s/~o preserve the exact selected discourse variable or named constant, not merely its noun class. A repeated exact proper name has the same constant; different names do not force inequality. Anonymous variables not selected for continuation are no longer available by a short reference. A demand to return to one later is outside this small channel unless the supplied source had explicitly named it.
full_teaching_grammar.names_without_kind: A quoted proper name may stand alone as an NP. It does not require an invented class word, and its spelling does not imply a noun kind, agent role, gender or number. This is a distinct contract from952's mandatory kind+name NP, not a silent removal inside952.

literal_names_and_physical_teaching_text.name_domain: The inherited83-character source inventory: a-z, A-Z, äöüßÄÖÜẞ, digits0-9, period, comma, semicolon, colon, exclamation, question mark, parentheses, hyphen, slash, apostrophe, double quote and ordinary space. Any other character is a declared unsupported input, not silently normalized.
literal_names_and_physical_teaching_text.Roman_name_encoding: Enclose the nonempty name in double quotes; double each literal double quote, and replace every name-internal ordinary space with underscore. Underscore is not an admitted source character, so its use is unambiguous. All other admitted name characters are literal inside quotes. Thus the encoded name is ONE external teaching group with no internal spaces; its complete spelling is paid. The reader undoubles internal quotes and changes each underscore back to an ordinary space.
literal_names_and_physical_teaching_text.external_spaces: Exactly one external blank separates adjacent complete groups. A quoted name is one NP group; this does not make its many written letters free or assert that it is one native word. Bare roots and inflected verbs are complete groups. No original source word boundaries are claimed to have been recovered by this semantic language.
literal_names_and_physical_teaching_text.line_rule_in_Roman_lesson: Wrap normally only at external spaces. If an individual group is too wide for the available line, start it on a fresh line, reserve one final cell and write a backslash there as the paid continuation mark. Resume the SAME group on the next line; repeat as needed. Before grammatical reading, remove backslash plus its immediate line break and join the two pieces. An unmarked line break stands for an external space. Backslash is excluded from every root and the admitted name inventory, so it cannot be mistaken for content. Splitting inside a doubled quote is harmless only because line reassembly precedes quote parsing.
literal_names_and_physical_teaching_text.carrier_debt: This is an explicitly Roman teaching notation, not a22-working-sign script. The full root alphabet, case-sensitive/rare name characters, quotation, underscore, tilde, inflection letters, negative marker and continuation mark still require a single paid22-sign representation. No old954 or956 carrier is imported. Consequently there is no claim that the current literal names, suffixes or line fragments have native lengths or frequencies.
literal_names_and_physical_teaching_text.written_cost: A finite word writes its full root plus tilde+one inflection letter, plus one exclamation if negative. Each name writes every admitted character, two enclosing quotes and one extra quote for each literal quote; each internal space becomes one written underscore. A broken group adds one backslash per continuation. All external blanks are written. These are Roman teaching-character costs, not measured working-glyph costs.

fol.meaning: a leaf-kind restriction on an existential witness; not an asserted exact global leaf count

vas.meaning: a vessel-kind restriction; no material, size or contents implied

aqa.meaning: water as a material referent; no counted cup, drop or portion is silently supplied

vel.meaning: first participant is warmer than second participant; direction is learned

complete_hand_examples.readback: There is a leaf x and a vessel y such that x touches y and that same leaf x is cold.
complete_hand_examples.trace: fol introduces S=x; vas introduces O=y; tat~s states touch(x,y) and explicitly carries x; nar~e states cold(x), then ends and clears the chain. The most recently written NP was vas, but it does not control the next subject.

complete_hand_examples.readback: There is a leaf x and a vessel y such that x touches y and that same vessel y is cold.
complete_hand_examples.trace: Only the inflection differs from the preceding example. ~o carries y, so replacing it by ~s changes the assertion. This is not merely another spelling of the same sentence.

complete_hand_examples.readback: There is a leaf x that the individual literally named Tava Ada does not touch, and that same leaf x is cold.
complete_hand_examples.scope: The leaf exists outside the predicate negation. No source states that Tava Ada does not exist, that there are no leaves, or that touching is prohibited. The name's internal space is recovered from the paid underscore.

complete_hand_examples.readback: There is a leaf x, and cold(x) is stated four times in order. The three identical middle-continuation words are legal and do not introduce four distinct leaves, numerical intensity or four events.
complete_hand_examples.obligation: Redundancy is permitted and preserved. This example supplies the source-side repetition property only, not a native value for any repeated form.

complete_hand_examples.readback: There is a cold leaf, and there is a cold vessel. They are separately quantified; the grammar does not identify them or impose inequality.
complete_hand_examples.boundary: The first ~e visibly ends the first chain. The next chain therefore has to write its first participant vas. No line or paragraph convention is used as a hidden sentence bit.

complete_hand_examples.reason: The unary predicate nar has no second participant. ~o cannot create an unseen object or choose another nearby noun. The input is invalid under this unchanged grammar.

human_learning_and_memory.learn: Each actual lexical kind/predicate and its spelling/valency; three productive verb inflections; predicate-negation scope; exact initial versus carried NP counts; name escaping and visible line continuation. Six entries suffice only for the examples, not for historical coverage.
human_learning_and_memory.remember: During a clause, its inherited or newly written S and any written O. After the verb, retain only the participant explicitly selected by its ending, or clear the slot at ~e. These are references into actually written source introductions, not a numerical table or private history cache.
human_learning_and_memory.purposeful_tradeoff: The inflection can save a repeated noun/name in a chain whose next clause concerns S or O. It loses956's branch stack and cannot return silently to an old anonymous participant. Not every graph of assertions fits this single-pivot order; source reordering or inventing labels is not free.
human_learning_and_memory.no_savings_claim: The ending itself, full open lexicon, every new NP/name, negative prefix, escaping and line continuation cost writing and learning. No corpus compression, plausible native distribution or complete source transfer is measured or asserted.

new_falsifiable_consequence_and_known_ob.semantic_consequence: In the fixed example pair, changing only ~s to~o must change the subject of nar from the leaf to the vessel. A nearest-NP resolver or a permanently fixed record topic cannot read both correctly. A unary ~o must be rejected. This distinguishes the declared grammatical controller from a generic carry mechanism.
triple_lemma: Consider three adjacent identical COMPLETE teaching groups W W W within one physical line, with no continuation fragments. A quoted name is one NP group because its internal spaces are escaped.
If W is nominal, at most two NPs can occur before a verb in an initial binary clause, and at most one can occur in a carried binary clause. Three identical NP groups are therefore invalid.
If W is binary finite, its next occurrence needs a written O in between, whether S was carried or a chain ended. It cannot occur three times without intervening groups.
If W is unary finite with ~e, its next occurrence needs an explicitly written new S in between. Unary ~o is invalid.
Thus every legal unbroken W W W consists of a unary predicate with the SAME continuation inflection ~s, possibly with the identical written negative prefix.
new_falsifiable_consequence_and_known_ob.conditional_physical_bound: Assume a SINGLE FIXED INJECTIVE rendering of complete teaching groups, independent of grammatical state, with each group retained whole; assume also that SAME becomes ONE fixed nonempty word-final working-sign string. Then identical written groups decode to identical teaching groups, so the triple lemma applies and all unbroken whole-word triples must share that exponent's last working sign under every global bijective renaming. The already supplied qokedy/sheol/okaiin/chol triple requirements include different final working signs y/l/n, so that narrow fixed-final realization cannot account for all of them under the inherited unit/group binding.
new_falsifiable_consequence_and_known_ob.scope_of_bound: The proof requires the stated grammar, an injective context-independent whole-group carrier, an invariant terminal exponent and complete unbroken-group correspondence. Mere sentence-level readability is NOT enough: if an added carrier made a noun and an inflected verb homographic, one written AAA could decode as N N V, so the lemma would not transfer from equal teaching words. No such homographic/context-sensitive carrier is supplied. The result identifies no native predicate, guarantees no source interpretation, tests no absent physical writer, and does not reject all morphological reference systems. A varied/internal exponent, changed grouping, noninjective contextual carrier or extra grammatical construction would be a changed contract; none is devised as a rescue here.
new_falsifiable_consequence_and_known_ob.decision: Retain the explicitly incomplete source-side module. Do not select a22-sign renderer, a hand-held source test, native experiment or statistical run from it. In particular do not build the simple uniform word-final SAME carrier after the known conditional obstruction.
